verdict.rationale: Bento documents OpenTelemetry trace ingestion: you point an OTel exporter at one endpoint with one auth header, and in TypeScript no Bento package is needed. It also offers a Python OTel transport for existing pipelines. However, the evidence covers only the sending side. Nothing shows Bento emitting or forwarding traces back out over OTLP to other backends. Running alongside another observability stack is not the same as exporting traces from Bento. missing for 10: documented OTLP export/egress of traces from Bento (the 'receive' side), explicit OTLP protocol/endpoint specs (gRPC vs HTTP, protobuf vs JSON), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send and receive traces over OpenTelemetry (OTLP) instead of a proprietary format

citations.quote: point its exporter at one endpoint with one auth header and the traces land in Bento. In TypeScript you can do this with no Bento package at all.
JavaScript's OpenTelemetry exporters can emit JSON, so you can send traces to Bento without installing any Bento package.
Every span from every framework, captured over OpenTelemetry.
Wire it into an OpenTelemetry pipeline directly when you already have one configured, and skip the analytics layer entirely.
